subject.title: [Feature]: Feishu Group Chat SubAgents for User-Specific Skills and Memory

question: Should OpenClaw extend Feishu dynamic agent creation from DMs to group senders as durable per-user agents, and what security, memory, routing, quota, and lifecycle model should govern it?
rationale: The implementation shape affects durable agent creation, plugin/channel ownership, memory isolation, authorization, resource limits, admin commands, and user-visible routing, so automation cannot safely choose the product contract.

options.title: Design an opt-in group dynamic-agent feature
options.body: Extend Feishu group handling with explicit opt-in config, sender authorization, isolated memory/workspaces, lifecycle/TTL/max-agent controls, routing tests, and live Feishu proof.

options.title: Keep current session scoping and manual bindings
options.body: Document groupSessionScope, manual agent bindings, and explicit subagent spawning as the supported path while leaving automatic per-sender group agents out of core for now.

options.title: Split into narrower canonical issues
options.body: Track identity collision, channel threading policy, and user skill preferences separately through #40194, #56307, and #48918 while deferring full group-agent orchestration.

recommendation.title: Design an opt-in group dynamic-agent feature
recommendation.body: Extend Feishu group handling with explicit opt-in config, sender authorization, isolated memory/workspaces, lifecycle/TTL/max-agent controls, routing tests, and live Feishu proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest recent owner signal for Feishu dynamic-agent routing and identity-sensitive behavior adjacent to the requested extension.
